root_idea.summary: The root centers on something breaking in upon a person or situation unexpectedly, without being anticipated.
root_idea.development: The basic notion of sudden onset develops into the adverbial noun بَغْتَة for an unforeseen occurrence or arrival.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested nominal بَغْتَة is a distinct lexical item meaning sudden or unforeseen occurrence.

senses.definition: Suddenly; unexpectedly, as something arrives or occurs without being anticipated.
senses.usage_conditions: An adverbial noun used with arrival, occurrence, coming, or encounter; in Quranic usage it describes an event overtaking people without prior awareness or expectation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A Christian festival, identified in one account as Easter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The identification is reported with some variation; another transmitted form is الباعوث.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Confounded or perplexed, unable to discern the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as a descriptive participial term, including in the expression لَا رَأْىَ لِمَبْغُوتٍ, “a confounded person has no sound judgment.”

lane_unit_coverage.note: The sudden, unexpected occurrence and surprise construction are covered by the Quranic sense.
Pointer-only entry referring back to the Form I entry.
Separate lexical name for a Christian festival.
Separate lexical term for a confounded or perplexed person.

cautions: Lane records variant forms and a variant Quran reading, while the public Quranic headword follows the QAC-attested form بَغْتَة.
